corrected_content.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane
$$
\mathbf{r}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -3 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{bmatrix}+t\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+s\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 5 \\ 7\end{bmatrix},\hspace{2em}t,\hspace{0.167em}s\in (-\mathrm{∞},\mathrm{∞}).
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
A normal vector is perpendicular to both direction vectors of the plane. Take their cross product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{n}&=\langle2,-4,3\rangle\times\langle1,5,7\rangle\\&=\langle(-4)(7)-(3)(5),\ (3)(1)-(2)(7),\ (2)(5)-(-4)(1)\rangle\\&=\langle-43,-11,14\rangle.\end{aligned}
$$

Indeed, $\mathbf{n}\cdot\langle2,-4,3\rangle=0$ and $\mathbf{n}\cdot\langle1,5,7\rangle=0$.
